{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Ricardo Cortez''' is an American mathematician and currently the Pendergraft William Larkin Duren Professor at [[Tulane University]].

== Professional career ==
Ricardo Cortez earned a BS in mechanical engineering in 1986 and a BA in applied mathematics in 1988 from [[Arizona State University]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|date=2019-02-16|title=Ricardo Cortez, Ph.D.|url=https://sse.tulane.edu/math/faculty/cortez|access-date=2020-08-04|website=School of Science & Engineering|language=en}}</ref>  In 1995, he earned his applied mathematics PhD from the [[University of California at Berkeley]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ricardo Cortez {{!}} Math Alliance: The National Alliance for Doctoral Studies in the Mathematical Sciences|url=https://mathalliance.org/mentor/ricardo-cortez/|access-date=2020-08-04|language=en-US}}</ref>  He was an instructor at the [[Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences]], which is [[New York University]]'s mathematics research school, from 1995 to 1998.<ref name=":1" />  Since 1998 he has been: Assistant Professor, Mathematics Department, Tulane University (1998–2001), Associate Professor, Mathematics Department, Tulane University 2001–2007. As of 2007 he is a professor, Mathematics Department, at Tulane University.<ref name=":1" />

== Awards and honors ==
Cortez was awarded the [[Blackwell–Tapia prize|Blackwell-Tapia Prize]] in 2012.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Grad alum Ricardo Cortez, now at Tulane, wins the prestigious Blackwell-Tapia Prize {{!}} Berkeley Graduate Division|url=https://grad.berkeley.edu/news/announcements/cortez/|access-date=2020-09-08|website=grad.berkeley.edu|date=June 2012 }}</ref> He was named to the 2021 class of fellows of the American Mathematical Society "for contributions in numerical methods for fluid dynamics and leadership in promoting opportunities in mathematical sciences for underrepresented groups".<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.ams.org/cgi-bin/fellows/fellows_by_year.cgi?year=2021|title=2021 Class of Fellows of the AMS|publisher=American Mathematical Society|accessdate=2020-11-02}}</ref>
